LLM auditresponse for restart-bettbox.hook:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The hook file is a standard systemd user‑upgrade hook that restarts the `bettbox` binary for each logged‑in user after an upgrade. It loops over `/run/user/*/` directories, retrieves the user name with `id -nu`, and runs `su` to execute `/usr/bin/bettbox --restart`. There are no network calls, encoded payloads, or unexpected file modifications. The quoting appears oddly escaped in the representation but reflects normal shell quoting for a hook script. This behavior aligns with typical AUR packaging practices for post‑install service restarts.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The .SRCINFO file contains only standard package metadata for bettbox-lite-bin, a network traffic routing tool built on the Mihomo core. The sources are pinned prebuilt .deb binaries fetched from the project's own GitHub releases page (https://github.com/appshubcc/Bettbox/releases/download/v1.19.8/...), which is the expected upstream location for a -bin package. Each source (two architecture-specific .deb files plus a local .hook and .install file) has a specific pinned sha256sum, not SKIP, so the downloaded artifacts are verifiable and reproducible. The dependencies (gtk3, libayatana-appindicator, libkeybinder3) and optional polkit dependency for TUN authorization are all consistent with the stated purpose of a GUI network-routing/DNS-debugging application. There are no eval, curl|bash, base64-decoded blobs, reverse shells, credential harvesting, or exfiltration constructs in this metadata file. No evidence of injected or malicious code was found.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>Standard .SRCINFO metadata with pinned checksums and upstream sources; no malicious indicators.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for bettbox.install:
<security_assessment>
  <decision>SAFE</decision>
  <details>
    The file defines a `post_install()` hook that sets `CORE_PATH="/usr/lib/bettbox/BettboxCore"`, checks if the file exists, and if so runs `/usr/bin/setcap 'cap_net_admin,cap_net_bind_service,cap_net_raw=+ep' "$CORE_PATH"` followed by `sync`. While `setcap` is normally applied to users or groups rather than to a directory, applying it here is unconventional but not inherently malicious; it merely attempts to grant privileged capabilities to the core package directory. The script contains no network requests, no eval/base64/curl/wget, and no code injection. This aligns with ordinary AUR post‑install hook patterns.
  </details>
  <evidence>
  </evidence>
  <summary>Post-install sets CAP_NET_ADMIN on core path via setcap and syncs.</summary>
</security_assessment>
